synthesized_by: orchestrator, after three analysts (civics-and-mechanism, energy-and-physical-reality, what-is-known-and-what-is-not) argued and red-teamed each other
thesis: Whether an AI data center on those acres makes a Fairbanks power bill smaller or bigger comes down to one variable, whether the load arrives with its own generation attached, and Alaska can still write that into the terms, because nothing has been awarded and the number that would settle it has never been published.
one_question: Does an AI data center on those acres make a Fairbanks power bill smaller or bigger?
valence_defense: All three analysts independently landed on curious and none was told the others' answers. Nothing has been awarded, the senior senator's objection is conditional and time-stamped, the mayor is on record about what the bases have given his town, and the central quantity is unpublished. Facts in that arrangement earn an investigation, not a verdict on a project that does not exist yet. The film still takes a position, and the position is about the PROCESS rather than the project: there is a third option between yes and no.
falsifiability: Publish a load figure for these parcels that sits inside existing Railbelt headroom, servable off current capacity with no new generation and no rate impact, and the thesis is dead: this is a real estate story, not a power story. Two further falsifiers, both things a reporter could go get: an RCA interconnection filing showing a selected developer served entirely from existing supply, or solicitation language putting the power obligation on the Air Force rather than the developer. The film names its own falsifier on screen, because a thesis that hides its test has not earned the right to be made.
supporting_facts: c6. Murkowski's objection is conditional and it names the INPUT, not the outcome: not a proponent because Alaska can't support them on an insecure energy base AT THIS TIME. She did not say the land. She said the power.
c15. Fairbanks already carries some of the nation's highest utility costs. A big fixed cost stack over a thin ratepayer base. That is why a new load is not neutral in either direction.

c1 and c11 together are the argument in two facts. The land is disclosed to the acre. The consumption is not disclosed at all. The offer is denominated in the abundant input while the scarce one goes unstated.

c14. The developer carries financing, permitting, construction and long-term operation. FOUR responsibilities are named and GENERATION IS NOT AMONG THEM. The structure PERMITS the good outcome and does not REQUIRE it. That gap is the finding, and it is what the ask is for.

c10. Nothing awarded as of September 15th. The lease terms and the permits that would carry a generation condition are still unwritten documents. A condition written after an award is a lawsuit. A condition written now is a term sheet.
fair_counter_it_must_honor: A Request for Lease Proposal precedes a project by design (c3), no developer had been selected (c10), and the developer carries permitting itself (c14). There may be no megawatt figure for the simple reason that there is no project. Demanding the number in September may be demanding a blank page for its weight, and a state that insists on a number before there is a project is a state that gets no projects. THE FILM CONCEDES THIS FULLY AND OUT LOUD, and the thesis survives because it never asks for the number. It asks for the date the number becomes public, which is answerable today with nothing designed.
second_movement: Fairbanks has said yes to a big federal neighbour before and was right to. Mayor Hopkins says the town was buoyed by defense spending and infrastructure when the F-35 squadron arrived (c12), and Hollister concedes the jets inside her own quote (c5). The recontextualising distinction: A FIGHTER WING IS A BUDGET AND A DATA CENTER IS AN APPETITE. The squadron arrived carrying its own appropriation. A load arrives carrying a demand curve, and a demand curve gets satisfied out of whatever supply is standing there.
act3_test: THE DIAGRAM THAT RUNS TWICE AND CANNOT RESOLVE. Build the Interior cost stack as one tall bar over a thin row of houses, which is c15. Add one enormous customer and run it both ways. Way one, the customer builds generation sized to its own load: the stack grows, the row grows faster, and the bar over the house SHRINKS. That is the pro-development case at full strength and it is the best energy news Interior Alaska could get, because new Railbelt generation is what Fairbanks has never been able to finance on its own ratepayer base. Way two, the customer draws on supply that already exists: same stack, new bidder, and the bar GROWS. Same land, same customer, opposite answer, one variable. Then put NOT DISCLOSED in the slot where the load figure goes and let the audience watch the diagram fail to resolve. The film does not narrate which is likelier.
what_an_alaskan_should_ask_for: Not the megawatts. Nobody can publish those yet, and asking invites a truthful shrug. Ask for the DATE: at what stage does the load figure become public, and is the lease executed before or after that stage. It needs no design decision, it can be answered today, and it is the pro-project ask rather than the hostile one, because a developer who intends to build is currently negotiating against a borrowed number it did not choose and cannot rebut.

runner_up_angles.angle: CIVICS: the borough's wish list is the smartest move in the story, not a confession of powerlessness, because an energy condition gets written into a lease term or a statute and never into a borough plat.
runner_up_angles.why_it_lost: It is right, and both the civics and the energy analysts converged on it independently, which is why it survives as the film's correction rather than its spine. It lost the spine because its central claim, that there is a next Alaska-controlled venue, could not be grounded in any statute in the safe set. Its own author said so: 'I can't name the statute, the claim set doesn't contain one.' A spine may not rest on a hypothesis dressed as law.

runner_up_angles.angle: INFORMATION: the missing item is not a quantity, it is a calendar, and a calendar can be published today without a single design decision being made.
runner_up_angles.why_it_lost: Not really lost. It IS the film's turn and its ask, absorbed whole. It did not take the spine because a disclosure-schedule thesis is a claim about paperwork, and the energy framing gives the same ask a stake a Fairbanks household can feel in its own bill.

runner_up_angles.angle: THE VACUUM: residents are objecting to a project whose size has never been published.
runner_up_angles.why_it_lost: Killed by the civics analyst on two counts and correctly. It is a description of an absence rather than a claim, so its only test is to wait. And it has an innocent explanation that Act 3 delivers cleanly: a lease solicitation precedes a project by design. The absence survives as EVIDENCE with a job to do, never as the thesis.

runner_up_angles.angle: COLD IS ALASKA'S EDGE: free air cooling makes the Interior one of the best places in America to run compute.
runner_up_angles.why_it_lost: Rejected on physics and on the safe set by the analyst who most wanted it. Cold cuts the COOLING load, and the compute pulls the same watts at forty below as it does in Phoenix, so the advantage lands on the smaller half of the bill. Proving it needs a PUE or a site comparison, and c11 is a verified absence while benchmarking against another named data center is banned. Refusing to do to the pro case what we refused to do to the against case is the whole discipline.

hard_constraints_carried_into_the_build: NO megawatt, water, acre-foot or project-size figure, ever, and no benchmark against another named data center to imply one.
The 'bring your own power' proposition attributed to gubernatorial candidates is NOT in claims.json. It may not be spoken, labelled or drawn. The film builds the generation argument on c14 alone.
SB 250 and the whole state-land / AIDEA track are UNVERIFIED and are OUT of this film. Keeping one story question is worth more than a second map.
Hollister's quote is a trail interview, never Assembly testimony. Hopkins is never cut as opposition.
No Alaska Native voice appears in any source, so the film implies neither support nor opposition. The Tanana is a subsistence watershed and carries no number.
